title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is buzzing with funding rounds and strategic partnerships, while legacy concerns about workforce pipelines and satellite servicing models linger. Meanwhile, the U.S. government continues to bolster its space resilience budget, albeit with some hiccups in hypersonic testing.

themes.title: Funding and Innovation Buzz
themes.body: Chinese startup Spark Space is making headlines with its electric-pump rocket engine tests and fresh funding. Meanwhile, True Anomaly's $190M Series C shows that investors are still keen on space ventures, despite the market's volatility.

themes.title: Workforce Pipeline Woes
themes.body: The space industry grapples with a workforce pipeline issue, as highlighted by initiatives like Project Patriot. As the sector expands, attracting and retaining skilled talent will be crucial for sustaining momentum.

themes.title: Satellite Servicing Models Evolving
themes.body: The satellite servicing economy is looking to carbon credit models for inspiration, suggesting a shift in how these services might be valued. This could pave the way for new business models that prioritize sustainability alongside profitability.

themes.title: Defense Budget Increases
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup has added $1.4B to the space resilience line, signaling a commitment to strengthening U.S. capabilities in the domain. However, the ongoing delays in hypersonic glide-vehicle tests raise questions about the effectiveness of this increased funding.
